articles.headline: Half of Premier League clubs face losing lucrative sponsors if unlicensed gambling firms banned
articles.snippet: Half of the Premier League’s 20 clubs have sponsorship or advertising deals with unlicensed gambling companies that could be illegal next year under plans being developed by the government. An eight-week consultation on proposals to ban sponsorship from gambling companies not licensed in the UK closes on Wednesday, with licensed operators such as Ladbrokes and William Hill pitted against the Premier League in a battle that could cost clubs tens of millions of pounds. The league is understood to be lobbying against a ban on the grounds that the services offered by primarily Asia-facing betting companies and online casinos are not available in the UK, although anyone with a VPN can open an account and place a bet in minutes.

articles.headline: Fitter, happier, more productive: Arsenal could hardly have started the season better
articles.snippet: Three league games played, three games won . For Arsenal this season could only have started better if Manchester City, who look like being one of their two most serious challengers, had dropped points. But it’s not just about results: Arsenal have been comfortably the better side in each of those three games, approaching each of them in very different ways.

articles.headline: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
articles.snippet: Everton need Grealish’s energy With 25 minutes to go against Manchester United, the Everton supporters had something to roar about as Jack Grealish made his return after rejoining on loan. The attacking midfielder remains universally popular thanks to his desire to entertain, getting the hosts back on their feet by creating dangerous situations within seconds of his arrival. Everton were limited in the final third for long periods as Thierno Barry sat on the periphery.

articles.headline: ‘Exceptional performance’: Arteta hails fightback win and says best yet to come
articles.snippet: Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal are capable of hitting even greater heights after the Premier League champions sent a statement to their title rivals by fighting back from a goal down to beat Chelsea on Sunday. Arteta’s side were under pressure after conceding for the first time this season when Morgan Rogers struck early at the Emirates Stadium, but the response to the setback was outstanding. Kai Havertz equalised before conjuring a brilliant dummy for a rejuvenated Martin Ødegaard to make it 2-1, ensuring that Arsenal moved level on points with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.

articles.headline: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Premier League – as it happened
articles.snippet: 6.55pm BST Match report: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea The first heavyweight encounter of the Premier League season was previewed in some quarters as the immovable object versus the irresistible force. Arsenal do not give an inch. Chelsea have been fun and free-scoring under Xabi Alonso.

articles.headline: Maitland-Niles stunner rescues late point for Everton against Manchester United
articles.snippet: Defiance serves David Moyes’s ­Everton well, especially when laced with a sense of indignation. At the end of a troubled week in the ­transfer market, and at the very end of a game when all seemed lost against ­Manchester United, they showed weaker in number need not translate to weaker in spirit. Ainsley Maitland-Niles, 19 ­minutes into his Everton debut, rescued a point for Moyes’s side with a stunning 25‑yard strike into Senne Lammens’s top ­corner with virtually the final kick of a game that slow-burned into an eruption.

articles.headline: High-flying Hull stay unbeaten by holding off Aston Villa in stalemate
articles.snippet: It’s never dull in Hull, as the saying goes in these parts, and after just three games the Premier League is proving to be quite some ride for Hull City supporters. Having embarrassed Manchester United here on the opening day and won at Coventry last weekend , this deserved point and third successive clean sheet merely reinforced Sergej Jakirovic’s belief that his men can beat the drop. You have to go back to Bolton’s excellent start in 2001-02 to find a promoted side who began the season with three straight victories.

articles.headline: Glasner claims VAR was ‘guessing’ after Forest are denied winner against Spurs
articles.snippet: Oliver Glasner argued there was insufficient evidence to disallow Neco Williams’s goal against Tottenham, accusing the video assistant referee Peter Bankes of guessing that the Nottingham Forest defender handled and said ruling it out weakens the officials’ authority. Midway through the second half, Williams stooped to head in on the goalline as Sandro Tonali attempted to hook the ball clear after Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected effort bobbled towards the net. Glasner conceded at least one angle showed Williams appeared to handle the ball, seemingly to protect himself as Tonali went to clear the ball with his left boot, but said the footage was too unclear to disallow the goal.

articles.headline: Manchester City 1-0 Coventry, Fulham 2-3 Crystal Palace and more: football clockwatch – as it happened
articles.snippet: 5.30pm BST That’s all for today’s Clockwatch. The new Premier League season has yet to settle but – oh, look – Manchester City and Arsenal are the top two so there is a degree of familiarity. Thanks for your company and emails; goodnight!

articles.headline: Enzo Le Fée penalty redemption rescues point for Sunderland at Brentford
articles.snippet: True redemption, perhaps, would have been to score with a Panenka, but Enzo Le Fée didn’t quite have the chutzpah for that. His duffed dink at Brentford in January was the low point of one of Sunderland’s two worst performances of the season, but he converted from the spot with eight minutes remaining to earn a draw in a battle of two physically aggressive and well-drilled teams who must both look at the chaos elsewhere and be thinking again of top-half finishes. It had seemed that it would be a tale of Brentford’s newfound strength in depth and a second-half turnaround as they overcame a rocky first period to have the better of the second after a triple change at half-time, having already lost their captain Nathan Collins to a calf strain.

articles.headline: Chilwell seals Crystal Palace comeback win after Mitchell double at Fulham
articles.snippet: The managers may have changed but the result stays the same. For the fourth successive trip to this part of west London, Crystal Palace returned over the river with a win as Pierre Sage got his reign off the mark in dramatic style. Their hero was Ben Chilwell, the former England left-back who was signed on deadline day from Strasbourg – this time permanently, after a loan spell in which he helped Palace win the FA Cup – after he came off the bench to volley home the winner.

articles.headline: Luka Vuskovic rides to the rescue for Brighton as Leeds fail to take chances
articles.snippet: What might have been; what should have been. By the end of this strange, enthralling match two exhausted teams trudged off the Amex Stadium turf wondering how they had not won it. Both sides’ ruminations were entirely legitimate.

articles.headline: Haaland edges Manchester City past Coventry as Fernández sparkles on debut
articles.snippet: Enzo Fernández started for Manchester City after Nico O’Reilly’s back injury during the warm-up and sparkled, showing why the club paid a British-record-equalling £125m for the midfielder. The winner came courtesy of Erling Haaland’s 300th goal in club football and Fernández had a key part, feeding Antoine Semenyo, whose cross from the right was crashed home. In the second half Coventry hammered away, but their wait for a first top-flight goal since Mustapha Hadji’s second in a 3-2 defeat at Aston Villa on 5 May 2001 goes on.

articles.headline: Jacob Ramsey comes in from the cold as Newcastle peg back Bournemouth
articles.snippet: Just as Bournemouth’s Alex Scott seemed to have succeeded in building a personal playground by the Tyne, another midfielder emerged from the shadows and stripped the shine from his afternoon. Since Matthias Jaissle succeeded Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s manager Jacob Ramsey has been largely shunted to the margins but the home substitute’s superbly executed 88th-minute equaliser ensured Scott and his teammates needed to settle for a point. For a third straight Premier League game Bournemouth’s new manager, Marco Rose, watched his side surrender a lead as much stellar passing and movement on Scott’s part was ultimately eclipsed.

articles.headline: Premier League news: Richarlison refused new contract, Alonso backs James in midfield
articles.snippet: De Zerbi defends treatment of Richarlison Roberto De Zerbi insisted he had no choice but to leave Richarlison out of Tottenham’s Premier League squad after the Brazilian declined the offer of a contract extension and repeatedly insisted he wanted to leave the club. Richarlison was Spurs’ leading scorer in the Premier League last season but did not feature in last weekend’s defeat to Newcastle amid discussions of a return to his former club Everton. He eventually rejected that move but, with Tottenham bringing in Omar Marmoush from Manchester City, there was no space for the 29-year-old in De Zerbi’s 25-man list of players he plans to use in the league this campaign.

articles.headline: Isak’s rapid double sinks Ipswich to give Andoni Iraola first Liverpool win
articles.snippet: A first win for Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool, the introduction of the latest star signing in Bradley Barcola making for a successful Friday night. Better yet, continuing signs that Alexander Isak, last year’s model, is coming back to life, his two, well-taken early goals securing the three points. That Cody Gakpo, Isak’s supplier, might have been at Manchester City or Tottenham had the transfer runes been right, added further to a sense of renewal.

articles.headline: A window tax to curb the Premier League’s big spenders
articles.snippet: Barney Ronay makes a lot of good points in his article about the recent Premier League transfer window ( Premier League money has lost all meaning amid chaotic spectacle of excess, 2 September ). I have one suggestion to add: a windfall tax. Levied on the spenders, it could raise money for the grassroots of the game and might act as an incentive to reduce the ludicrous fees being splashed around, which, as Ronay points out, are eventually paid for by the fans.

articles.headline: Lucas Herrington staying grounded at Hull City despite meteoric rise: ‘It’s pretty crazy’
articles.snippet: On the opening day of the Premier League season, with just over an hour gone in Hull City’s clash with Manchester United, Lucas Herrington got up off the bench. With the Tigers 2-0 up, manager Sergej Jakirović turned to the 18-year-old Australian to replace injured goalscorer Nobel Mendy with a clear role in mind. “I knew the job that had to be done,” Herrington says, two weeks after his debut.

articles.headline: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
articles.snippet: Can Wirtz find his best for Liverpool? Florian Wirtz is easing himself into his second season at Liverpool after a forgettable first. There were signs of promise against Nottingham Forest , where he set up the second equaliser and would have had a goal of his own if not for an offside in the buildup.

articles.headline: Mike Dean claims he played secret games for a laugh while refereeing matches
articles.snippet: The former Premier League referee Mike Dean claims he used to take part in secret challenges while officiating, including trying to stay in the centre circle for as long as possible, as he confessed to “just joking about” during matches. The remarks, made by one of the most well-known officials in the English game, have been met with bemusement by refereeing officials who say there is no evidence of any such behaviour having ever taken place. Dean was a member of the select group of referees for more than two decades before he retired in 2022 and a brief spell as a video assistant referee followed.

articles.headline: Premier League money has lost all meaning amid chaotic spectacle of excess
articles.snippet: There was a research study a few years back into a key period in the life of the TV show Location, Location, Location. You know the one. Half an hour of mid-morning drift.

articles.headline: Premier League transfer talking points: three things we learned from the data
articles.snippet: Premier League clubs have invested more than £3.4bn in players this summer, an increase of 11.9% on last year. There are three aspects of this enormous spending worthy of closer scrutiny. Priorities on player age have changed Premier League clubs are spending less on players in the peak 24-27 age band even though those players are increasingly the core of their selections.

articles.headline: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
articles.snippet: Arsenal Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund.
